title: Zippered Makeup Pouch
summary: A lined, boxed pouch with a neat zipper and tabbed ends.
description: Your first zipper, done the easy way. The sandwich method attaches outer, zipper and lining in one seam, and fabric tabs give clean ends. Boxed corners make it stand up on the counter. Great for makeup, pencils or chargers.
customNote: Panels follow finished size + depth + seam allowances. The zipper must be at least 4 cm longer than the top edge; tabs stay the same size.

tools.name: Zipper foot
tools.why: Lets you stitch next to the zipper teeth.
substitutes: Adjustable needle position with standard foot (harder)

tools.name: Sewing clips
tools.why: Holding layers around the zipper — pins distort it.

materials.name: Outer fabric
materials.why: Forms the outside and zipper tabs.

materials.name: Medium fusible interfacing
recommended: Fusible fleece for a padded pouch
materials.why: Gives the pouch body so it stands up. Skip for canvas outers.

materials.name: Nylon coil zipper
materials.why: Coil zippers can be cut to length and sewn over.

pieces.name: Outer panel
markings: Cut a {D/2} square from both bottom corners

pieces.name: Lining panel
markings: Cut a {D/2} square from both bottom corners

pieces.name: Interfacing panel
pieces.notes: Cut without seam allowance to reduce bulk; centre it on the outer panel.

steps.title: Press fabrics and check your zipper
steps.text: Press both fabrics. Measure your zipper: the teeth (not the tape) must be at least as long as the measurement shown — it gets trimmed later, so longer is fine.
steps.beginner: Coil zippers (with a plastic spiral) can be cut with ordinary scissors. Metal-tooth zippers can't be sewn over — don't use them for this project.
steps.alt: A coil zipper with its minimum length dimensioned.

steps.title: Cut the outer panels and tabs
steps.text: Fold the outer fabric lengthwise and cut two outer panels and the two zipper tabs following the layout.
warnings: Keep blades closed and pointed away from you when not cutting.
steps.alt: Cutting layout for the outer fabric with two panels and two small tabs.

steps.title: Cut the lining panels
steps.text: Fold the lining and cut two lining panels the same size as the outer panels.
steps.alt: Cutting layout for the lining fabric.

steps.title: Cut the interfacing
steps.text: Cut two interfacing panels. They are smaller than the outer panels — this keeps the seams less bulky.
steps.beginner: Interfacing has a glue side (slightly shiny or bumpy). It doesn't matter which way up you cut it.

steps.title: Cut the corner squares
steps.text: Cut a square from both bottom corners of every outer and lining panel, measured from the raw edges.
steps.alt: A panel with squares cut from both bottom corners.

steps.title: Fuse the interfacing
steps.text: Centre an interfacing panel, glue side down, on the wrong side of each outer panel, 1 cm in from every edge. Cover with a damp pressing cloth and press for 10–15 seconds in each spot without sliding. Let them cool flat.
steps.beginner: Lift the iron and put it down in the next spot, overlapping slightly. Sliding causes wrinkles that can't be undone once cool.
steps.expert: Fuse interfacing to outer WS, 1 cm inset.
warnings: Hot iron and steam — use a pressing cloth and keep fingers clear.
steps.alt: Interfacing centred on the wrong side of an outer panel with a one-centimetre margin and an iron above.

steps.title: Add tabs to the zipper ends
steps.text: Trim the zipper so that, with the tabs attached, it spans the length shown. Fold each tab in half, wrong sides together (short ends meeting), then open, fold each short end in to the centre crease and fold again so it wraps the zipper end. Edgestitch across each tab.
steps.beginner: Before trimming, move the zipper pull to the middle so it doesn't fall off. Sew slowly over the coil; hand-turn the wheel if needed.
steps.expert: Trim zip; wrap ends with folded tabs; total span = W + D.
warnings: Move the pull to the centre before cutting the zipper.
steps.alt: A zipper with a folded fabric tab stitched over each end, the total length dimensioned.

steps.title: Sew the first side of the zipper
steps.text: Lay one outer panel right side up. Place the zipper face down on it, tape edge level with the top edge, centred. Lay a lining panel right side down on top, matching the top edge. Clip. With the zipper foot, sew through all layers 1 cm from the edge. When you near the pull, stop with the needle down, lift the foot, slide the pull behind the foot, and continue.
steps.beginner: Three layers: outer (face up), zipper (face down), lining (face down). The zipper is sandwiched with its teeth facing the outer.
steps.expert: Outer RS up / zip face down / lining RS down; sew 1 cm with zipper foot.

els.text: outer face up · zipper face down · lining face down

steps.alt: Outer panel, zipper and lining stacked along the top edge with stitching one centimetre down.

steps.title: Sew the second side
steps.text: Fold the outer and lining away from the zipper. Repeat the sandwich on the other zipper tape with the second outer panel (right side up, under the zipper) and second lining panel (right side down on top). Line up the side edges with the first side, clip and sew.
steps.expert: Repeat on the other tape, aligning sides.
steps.alt: Both outer panels attached to either side of the zipper, edges aligned.

steps.title: Press and topstitch along the zipper
steps.text: Press the outer and lining away from the zipper on both sides so the fabric folds sit 3 mm from the teeth. Topstitch along each side, 3 mm from the fold, through outer and lining.
steps.beginner: Topstitching stops the fabric from getting caught in the zipper pull.
steps.alt: Topstitching lines just beside both sides of the zipper.

steps.title: Sew outer to outer, lining to lining
steps.text: OPEN THE ZIPPER at least halfway. Bring the two outer panels right sides together and the two lining panels right sides together, with the zipper folded towards the lining (teeth facing the lining). Clip. Sew down the sides and across the bottoms with a 1 cm seam, leaving an 8 cm gap in the lining bottom and leaving all corner squares open.
steps.beginner: If you forget to open the zipper, you can't turn the pouch. At the zipper, make sure the tabs point towards the lining and the zipper tapes lie flat.
steps.expert: Open zip; outer RST + lining RST; sew all round except corners and 8 cm lining gap.
steps.alt: Outer panels and lining panels each placed right sides together side by side, sewn around except a gap in the lining bottom.

steps.title: Box all four corners
steps.text: Box each of the four corners (two outer, two lining): match the side seam to the bottom seam, flatten, and sew across with a 1 cm seam. Backstitch.
steps.alt: A corner pinched with seams aligned and stitched across to box it.

args.label: turn right side out through the lining gap

steps.title: Turn, close the gap and shape
steps.text: Turn the pouch right side out through the lining gap and through the open zipper. Push out the corners. Close the lining gap with edgestitching or a ladder stitch and push the lining inside.
steps.alt: The pouch being pulled through the lining gap.

steps.title: Final press
steps.text: Press the pouch, using a rolled towel inside to shape it. Check the zipper runs smoothly end to end.
steps.expert: Press over a towel roll; test zipper.
steps.alt: The finished pouch with its zipper highlighted.
